analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md. The head adds a Context section (head lines 25-171) describing the unregistered NemotronSuper local paths: bridge builder, load transaction, image binding, optional local HTTP hook, concurrency and prefill knobs, a resident hybrid prefix-checkpoint bank, and opt-in MTP. A later hunk (base ~729, head ~876-877) was only partly visible. The base-only units (lines 831-1204) were reviewed and show no changed security behavior. No source, config or endpoint changes were supplied, so no control regression is established.

Threat-model observations for later passes:
1. The new text says DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1 enables a resident recurrent checkpoint bank with the "local unscoped cache scope" (head lines 131-145). T-041 states production has no RAM prefix tier and scopes the cache via coordinator-authored cacheSalt. The doc says the owner is unregistered, has no HTTP route, and "No production caller installs it" (head lines 105, 34-35). If the underlying code ever becomes production-reachable, T-041/SEC-035 would need an update covering an unscoped cross-tenant TTFT oracle. I see no evidence of that here.
2. The optional NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP hook (head lines 100-105) is described as reusing the authenticated local app. The authentication itself is not shown and was not verified.
3. The image decode and encoded ingress (head lines 74-92) takes untrusted base64 PNG/JPEG. The doc says limits are checked before raster allocation. That is a claim in prose and was not verified against source.

No dependent source files were supplied. The claims above are unverified contracts, not findings.
